title: Isomers of Butane (C₄H₁₀) — Structural Isomerism
description: Discover how identical chemical formulas can produce completely distinct molecular structures.

steps.prompt: Butane has the chemical formula C₄H₁₀. How many structural isomers (different carbon chain arrangements) can be constructed?
steps.explanation: Correct! Butane has exactly two structural isomers: normal butane (a straight chain of 4 carbons) and 2-methylpropane (isobutane, with a 3-carbon chain and a central methyl branch).

steps.prompt: Examine carbon's tetravalency (4 bonds). Each internal carbon bonds to 2 carbons and 2 hydrogens, while terminal carbons bond to 3 hydrogens.
steps.explanation: Compounds having identical molecular formulae but different structural arrangements are called structural isomers.

steps.prompt: Which isomer of butane has a lower boiling point and why?
options: Isobutane because branching creates a spherical shape with smaller surface area and weaker van der Waals forces
Both boil at exactly the same temperature
steps.explanation: Isobutane is more compact and globular, reducing contact surface area and decreasing intermolecular van der Waals forces, which lowers its boiling point (-11.7 °C vs -0.5 °C for n-butane).
